passage: Friday evening, the accounts office was half empty when Tanvir stopped at Sudha's desk. "You're my best analyst. Nobody else can fix this month-end file. The whole team will suffer if you're not in tomorrow." Sudha's stomach dropped. Tomorrow was her cousin's engagement lunch. She felt guilty already, and a little flattered too. She had heard the same praise three weekends in a row, and her review still said nothing about extra work. "Sir, will this be counted in my review? And can I take Monday morning off?" Tanvir waved his hand. "We'll see, we'll see." Sudha picked up her bag. "I can do two hours tomorrow morning, not the whole day. After that I have a family event." He frowned, but nodded. 😔

qa.a: It was Sudha's cousin's engagement lunch.

qa.q: What mix of feelings did Sudha have when Tanvir praised her?
qa.a: She felt guilty and a little flattered at the same time, and her stomach dropped.

qa.q: What did Sudha do to test whether the praise was real?
qa.a: She asked whether the extra work would count in her review and whether she could take Monday morning off, then offered a clear limit of two hours.

qa.q: How might Tanvir see Sudha's answer?
qa.a: He may feel annoyed, since he frowned, but he still agreed, which suggests her limit was clear enough to accept.

grounding: A boss uses praise and guilt to get extra work; the worker checks the reward and negotiates a clear limit.

passage:
So, Didi, you asked why I finally said no to Omkar sir. Here's the thing. Every Friday at 5 he'd come to my desk: "Naveen, you're the only one I trust with this. You're like my right hand." And I'd glow, and stay till nine doing someone else's report.
When I once said I had plans, he sighed: "I thought you were loyal to this team." I felt so guilty I cancelled.
After six months of being his right hand, I checked. No raise. No new title. The person whose reports I was finishing got promoted.
So last Friday, when he started, "Naveen, only you can...", I said, "Sir, thank you. I can take it on Monday morning, or I can take it tonight if it comes with the team-lead role we discussed in January. Which works?"
He blinked. He said Monday. Nothing exploded.
Saying no isn't disloyal. It's just honest. That's what I'm learning, me, Naveen, former right hand.

qa.q: When would Omkar sir come to Naveen's desk?
How did Naveen feel when Omkar sir hinted at disloyalty?
qa.a: So guilty that Naveen cancelled the plans.

qa.q: How did Naveen negotiate clearly last Friday?
qa.a: Naveen thanked Omkar sir and offered two options: Monday morning, or that night along with the team-lead role discussed in January.

qa.q: How might Omkar sir have seen Naveen's reply?
qa.a: As a surprise; he blinked and chose Monday, seeing that praise alone no longer worked.

grounding: Shows a boss using praise and guilt to extract extra work, checking whether the reward is real, and negotiating clearly without feeling disloyal.

passage:
Week 1: At the NGO's Pune office, Sharmila ma'am told Ojas, "You're the heart of this team," and asked him to run the weekend donor event, unpaid, "just this once". He said yes, warmed by the praise.
Week 3: "Just this once" had happened three times. When Ojas mentioned his sister's engagement, Sharmila ma'am said, "I thought you cared about the children we serve." He went home guilty and angry at once.
Week 5: Before the next request, he looked at what had actually come of it: no day off in return, not even a mention in the monthly report. He asked for ten minutes with her. "I do care about this work. I'm happy to do one weekend event a month if I get a weekday off in return. Otherwise I can't." She was quiet, then said, "Fine. Put it in the leave register." He did, and went to the engagement.

qa.q: What did Sharmila ma'am call Ojas in week 1?
How did Ojas feel after the remark about the children?
qa.a: Guilty and angry at the same time.

qa.q: How did Ojas check the reward and negotiate?
qa.a: He looked at what had come of it (no day off, no mention), then offered one weekend a month only with a weekday off in return.

qa.q: How might Sharmila ma'am see Ojas's terms?
qa.a: She was quiet, perhaps surprised, but agreed and told him to use the leave register.

grounding: Illustrates praise and guilt used to get extra unpaid work, checking whether the reward is real, and negotiating clearly.
